title: PowerToys Runs at Startup but Doesn't Create Tray Icons
summary: Working modules with a missing startup tray icon fit a shell-registration race, but elevation and overflow state are unconfirmed.

evidence: PowerToys 0.102.3001 starts at Windows 11 login; Command Palette hotkeys still work while the main tray icon is absent.
Launching PowerToys again makes the icon appear. No diagnostic attachment, elevation state or tray-overflow comparison is supplied.
judgment.recommended_action: Capture the missing-icon state before relaunch and compare with #51463; avoid another installation or configuration reset.
judgment.rationale: This is not evidence that PowerToys failed to start. Existing related reports narrow the investigation, but do not prove an exact duplicate or shipped fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A recovery correction is conditional on confirming failed shell registration; no covering implementation was found in the bounded issue/fork records.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: initial Shell_NotifyIcon registration loses a startup race with Explorer. An overflow-hidden icon or another lifecycle path remains possible; elevation and the first registration result are unknown.
proposed_fixes.title: tray-registration recovery investigation
verification: Reboot with ordinary and elevated startup and delayed Explorer readiness.
Check both visible tray and overflow, ensuring one icon eventually appears without a second PowerToys launch.

confidence.rationale: The source identifies a plausible boundary, but this pass did not reproduce the failing transition. The accompanying diagnostic action distinguishes competing explanations.

plan: Reproduce the login timing with a working module and confirm whether NIM_ADD failed.
Compare the elevated startup path with #51463 before opening separate implementation work.
If registration failure is confirmed, design bounded recovery independent of an incidental window-position message; preserve single-icon and Explorer-restart behavior.

initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and empty discussion/timeline; searched upstream startup/tray reports and matching fork traces.
runner/tray_icon.cpp tracks NIM_ADD success, registers TaskbarCreated and retries after WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING; the code explicitly recognizes an Explorer-not-ready startup race.

Open #51463 describes the elevated-startup delay/reset issue and the same running-modules/missing-icon symptom. Older #41796, #35823 and #35475 contain related reports but are closed; none establishes this new report as fixed.
Focused tray-icon history concerns session shutdown, icon badges and telemetry rather than a demonstrated correction for this startup report.
Reassessed the complete current issue discussion and timeline, including the latest maintainer labels. Label changes alone do not satisfy unanswered evidence requests or prove a repair.
inferences: A delayed shell registration is plausible because a second launch restores the icon, but this does not exclude overflow state.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: After a login with the icon missing, check the tray overflow and administrator setting without restarting PowerToys, then comment /bugreport. If Settings/tray cannot open, run BugReportTool.exe from the PowerToys installation directory before relaunch.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes hidden-icon configuration from failed shell registration and determines whether the elevated-startup precedent applies.
information_gaps.information: A startup report captured before relaunch, whether the icon is absent from tray overflow too, and whether Always run as administrator is enabled.

issue_context.analysis: Use the existing tray-registration and startup ownership path; do not promise a delay-only fix or classify a closed historical report as a shipped correction.

actions.label: Approve conditional tray-registration recovery investigation plan
Capture missing startup icon before relaunch

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that Command Palette still responds and a second launch restores the icon; that narrows this away from a total startup failure. After the next affected login, please confirm whether the icon is also absent from the tray overflow and whether Always run as administrator is enabled, then comment `/bugreport` before relaunching PowerToys. If neither Settings nor the tray can open, run BugReportTool.exe from the installation directory first. This distinguishes hidden-icon state from shell-registration failure and the elevated-startup case in #51463.
